title: Mandate
description: A sentence of intent, the knobs derived from it, and why each knob has the value it has. Kept in its own file because the policy schema is closed: a mandate cannot be a block inside policy.yaml. The mandate says what was asked for and how it was read; policy.yaml stays the sole authority on what execution is allowed to do.

text.description: The mandate in the words it was given in. Kept verbatim so the derivation can be re-read against the request rather than against a paraphrase of it.

derived_by.description: Who or what turned the text into knobs. A model id when an agent derived it, a human identifier when a person did. Not a signature and not an authorization: it records provenance, and validate-mandate trusts none of it.

policy_path.description: Path to the derived policy, relative to the mandate file.

policy_hash.description: sha256 of the policy file's bytes, as 'sha256:<64 hex>'. Binds the mandate to one exact policy: an edited policy no longer matches the rationale that argued for it, and validate-mandate fails rather than letting the two drift apart silently.

strategy.description: Construction rule the mandate resolves to. Composites are allowed here, unlike inside a sleeve tier.

rationale.description: One entry per knob the derivation moved off its default. This is the readable half of the artifact: without it a mandate is a config file that claims to have been reasoned about.

StrategyParams.title: StrategyParams
StrategyParams.description: Parameters for the chosen strategy. Only the sleeve ladder is described structurally, because it is the only one whose shape a mandate is expected to derive; other strategies pass their scalar params through.

Tier.title: Tier
Tier.description: One band of the sleeve ladder. Mirrors what core.strategies.library._tier_specs accepts, closed here so a typo in a derived mandate is caught by validation rather than silently ignored by the strategy.

min_score.description: Inclusive lower bound of the band, and also its safety rank: weight released by a dropped tier may only move to a tier with a strictly higher min_score.

max_score.description: Exclusive upper bound. The top band uses a value above 1 to include a perfect score.

weight.description: Target share of the book for this band.

strategy.description: Construction rule inside the band. Flat strategies only; composites are rejected so dispatch stays finite.

min_positions.description: Names the band must hold before it may carry its target at all. A band that cannot reach it is dropped whole, not held small. Do not set one that has not been checked against the live shelf: when the band that comes up short is the safest one, its weight redistributes downward and the book gets riskier than it would have been with no floor.

Bands.title: Bands
Bands.description: How far the book may drift from its targets before a rebalance is worth its costs. These are the cost lever: on a stable book the drift check answers 'no' and no agent runs.

weight_drift_bps.description: Per-instrument tolerance, in basis points of the book.

sleeve_drift_bps.description: Per-sleeve tolerance, in basis points of the book. Wider than the per-instrument band in a sensible mandate: names inside a band are substitutes for each other, so the band's total is the number the mandate actually asked for.

min_uplift_bps.description: How much better a same-sleeve instrument must pay before switching to it is worth the round trip, in basis points of APY. The other bands ask whether the book moved away from its targets; this one asks whether the shelf moved underneath a book that did not. Optional: omit it and the opportunity check reports itself unevaluated rather than assuming a tolerance. It is a floor on rate only -- `drift` additionally requires the switch to repay its own execution cost within the year, which is arithmetic and not a matter of mandate policy.

knob.description: Dotted path to the setting being justified, e.g. 'caps.min_effective_positions' or 'strategy_params.tiers'.

value.description: The value chosen. Any JSON type, since knobs range from numbers to tier lists.

because.description: Which part of the mandate text this value answers, and why this value rather than the default. A restatement of the value is not a reason.
